source_findings.finding: The main-text standard U-statistic display has non-strict inequalities 1<=i1<=...<=id<=n, while the following C(n,d) description says distinct elements. Preserve both; do not silently replace the display by a strict-index sum.

The printed omega uses z1 vee z3 > z2 wedge z4 and z1 vee z2 > z3 wedge z4 in its second and fourth indicators. Preserve those min/max directions rather than importing a standard sign-covariance kernel.
Definition 1(c) contains an extra comma between the third and fourth X arguments. Preserve or explicitly record this typographic source artifact; do not reinterpret it as a fifth argument.

S squared is described as the variance of T-natural and then used for the leading-term variance (5). Under local alternatives the source additionally gives S_h squared = var(sum h2) = Delta_h^(-2) S squared. Retain these source passages and their regimes separately instead of asserting that the null product-of-marginal-variances formula is exact under alternatives.

Assumption 1 has two limits as p diverges and two parallel limits as q diverges. Theorem 1 requires max(p,q) to diverge. Preserve the conditional dimension regimes; do not impose divergence of both dimensions.

Theorem 4 invokes conditions (8)-(10). Its theta, zeta, G_h projection sums and S_h are defined immediately before those conditions. The contamination model (11) and Proposition 4 are examples, not additional theorem assumptions.
Theorem 3 needs V(z1,z2)=V1(x1,x2)V2(y1,y2) defined just before it; preserve its full constant clause on page 10.

Theorem 5 is restricted to bivariate Gaussian marginals; it does not impose the independence null or the asymptotic moment condition. Its M_h functions and monotonicity/extrema are bound within the theorem, rather than pre-existing assumptions.
